old: provide three months’ pay for the army, and add ten thousand measures of grain.
new: and with it to provide three months’ pay for the army, and to add tens of thousands of measures of grain.
reason: δοῦσι…μισθοδοτῆσαι: the fifty talents are the three months’ pay. Bare μυριάδας rendered “tens of thousands”; a numeral may have dropped out, so the editor may add [...].

old: withdrew, as ordered, to his quarters
new: withdrew, as ordered, [...]
reason: εἰς ἱμάτιον… is corrupt and gapped; ‘to his quarters’ is invented. Destination left as [...]; editors’ conjectures (e.g. Apamea) belong in a note, not the text.

old: [...] and for thirty years after that period, was continually being refined
new: [...] and thirty years later; from that time on it was continually being refined
reason: ἔτεσιν ὕστερον is a point in time, not a duration. ‘and thirty’ kept literal: the lacuna probably hides the rest of a compound numeral, so the full figure is unknown.

old: But Hieronymus, already leaning strongly toward the Carthaginians, said
new: But Hieronymus, while the Carthaginian envoys were still close at hand [...], said
reason: Bracketed εἴτ᾽ ἐν μισειόντων is corrupt; kept only the secure sense (envoys present, confirmed by παρόντας below) and marked the corruption; ‘leaning toward’ dropped as invented.

old: afterward to make his move, by a circuitous route, toward Syria
new: afterward to make his move toward Syria without any advance warning
reason: δίχα προόδου is obscure (literally “without advance/going forward”). Took it as suddenness, following ἄφνω καὶ παραδόξως; “circuitous route” has no basis in the Greek.

old: Hannibal could say nothing against the daring and practical force of the proposal
new: [...] Hannibal could say nothing against the daring and practical force of the proposal
reason: Source marks a break (…) before Ἀννίβας δέ, though the sense runs on. Marked to avoid smoothing; remove only if the collated text shows no gap.

old: wait there quietly with his force
new: wait there with his force, lingering as if at [...]
reason: ὡς ἐπὶ * πρεπίου is corrupt (likely a lost place or occasion); ἐνσχολάσαντα = lingering. ‘Quietly’ has no basis in the Greek.

old: especially along the coast, among the Etruscans and the Gauls
new: especially among the Etruscans and the Gauls
reason: The edition brackets [τὴν παλαίαν] as spurious, so it is omitted. “Along the coast” rests only on the conjecture παραλίαν and is not in the text.

old: not realizing that falsehood is no less present in those who in their histories pass over in silence what actually happened than in those who misstate it
new: not realizing that falsehood is no less present among those who [...] what actually happened [...] writing in their histories
reason: Lacuna between γεγονότα and γράφοντας; the usual supplement (suppressing facts vs. writing what did not happen) fits but is not transmitted; footnote it if wanted.

old: and by this Masinissa quickly stripped the Carthaginian left wing of its mounted support.
new: [...] of Masinissa’s men [...] the Carthaginian left wing was quickly stripped bare.
reason: Lacuna before τῶν περὶ τὸν Μασαννάσαν; ‘by this’ is invented. Kept ἐψιλώθη passive; how the genitive was construed is lost, so left unresolved.

old: but he struck the enemy below the waterline
new: but he struck the enemy ship under the [...]
reason: ὑπὸ τὰ * βίαχα is corrupt; ‘below the waterline’ is only an inference from the ἔξαλον contrast, so the noun is marked lost.

old: For he was well aware of the embassies being sent to Rome against him, now that affairs in Libya had come to an end.
new: For he was well aware of the embassies being sent to Rome against him, [...] for this reason affairs in Libya were at an end.
reason: Lacuna (* **) before διόπερ is marked; διόπερ means ‘therefore’, not ‘now that’. The clause may be a misplaced excerptor’s note: left as transmitted.

old: the Scipios and Lucius
new: Scipio and Lucius
reason: Σκιπίωνα is singular; kept as transmitted. The apposition “naval victors” fits neither cleanly; probably corrupt (L. Scipio plus L. Aemilius Regillus?). Editor may add a note.

old: In particular Leon son of Hicesias seemed to have spoken well in other respects
new: For Leon son of Cichesias, speaking after Damon, seemed to have spoken well in other respects
reason: καὶ γάρ = ‘For’; μετὰ Δάμων᾽ kept. The line is garbled (lowercase λέων); the Greek gives Κιχησίου = Cichesias (Livy: Hicesias). Translator may annotate.

old: he took measures to prevent any importation of funds gathered from outside.
new: he [...] the bringing-in of funds procured from outside.
reason: περιεβα... is truncated and no μή survives. The context suggests he prevented imports, but that negative is not asserted; the gap is marked instead.

old: but that in his whole strength and conduct he deserved to be stripped of power and punished
new: but that he had [...] with his whole strength toward the overthrow of Roman dominion, and deserved correction and punishment
reason: Verb lost after ὅλην; τῆς ἀρχῆς taken as Rome’s rule (Gnaeus is accusing him of hostility), not his deposition; ‘and conduct’ removed as invented.

old: disapproved of both the treatment of the walls and the killings at Compasium
new: disapproved of both the [...] of the walls and the abolition [...] of those killed at Compasium
reason: συντελέσει* is flagged as corrupt (demolition is expected), so the noun is marked as a gap. καταλύσει is kept as ‘abolition’, and the lacuna after it is marked.

old: Calling him king and offspring of gods, they said that if he abused such a name he might perhaps obtain some pity and pardon for what had happened
new: Calling this man king and blood of gods [...] making use of [...] that they would obtain some pity and pardon for [...] the king [...]
reason: Damaged papyrus: only surviving words kept, gaps marked. The conditional, “perhaps” and “what had happened” were invented. The rest of the paragraph after this span also smooths over gaps.

old: yet it would have been more kingly not to be the first to break faith, but rather to let others violate agreements before he did so himself
new: [...] and indeed more kingly [...]; for it was better to be betrayed by others than himself to be the first to break his pledges, and indeed to be wronged rather than [...] and they say that men [...] share the sufferings of the unjust [...] to be nearest to the divine nature [...] to obtain honors [...]; for no god is the first to do harm to men [...]
reason: Papyrus fragments: only scraps survive, so the invented whole judgment is gone. ἀδίκοις = ‘the unjust’, not ‘the wronged’; ανους read as the abbreviation for ἀνθρώπους.

old: one must be of one mind with the Romans in present circumstances
new: circumstances [...] one [...] to the Romans
reason: καιροῖς ἕνα Ῥωμαίοις has no verb and ἕνα may be corrupt; only the surviving words are given, nothing supplied; ‘be of one mind’ is invented.

old: the remaining one to Tenedos under a commander named Timagoras
new: the remaining one to Tenedos, on which [...] Timagoras sailed as commander
reason: The text has a gap (*) before Τιμαγόρας. It may have held “another” or a different name, so the gap is marked and not resolved.

old: only a very few Greeks were driven into utter folly at the crisis of the action
new: only a very few Greeks acted with utter want of judgment at the crisis of the action
reason: Passive ἠλογήθησαν is ambiguous: ‘were utterly disregarded’ is possible. I chose ‘acted irrationally’, which fits the ἀλογιστία context. ‘Driven’ has no support either way. Flag for translator.

old: That embassy also succeeded in persuading the Rhodians to join the war.
new: He also persuaded the Rhodians to join in the war.
reason: The subject is Perseus, not the embassy. The aorist is rendered as written. It conflicts with Rhodes’ later conduct (chs. 10–11), so a conative reading (“tried to persuade”) or corruption is possible.

old: as I have explained in my discussion of public speaking
new: [as is set down in the section on public speeches]
reason: The Greek brackets this passive cross-reference, probably the excerptor pointing to his collection On Speeches; it is not Polybius speaking in the first person. Brackets kept.

old: the siege of Phanoteia or Coroneia or Haliartus
new: the siege of Phanoteia and Coroneia and [...]
reason: Third name survives only as ‘...ε...οῦ’; ‘Haliartus’ is conjecture and is removed; καί rendered ‘and’ as in the Greek.

old: seeing on the one hand that the division had been completely settled
new: seeing on the one hand that the division [...] had been completely settled
reason: Lacuna falls between μερισμὸν and γεγονότα; a lost qualifier (possibly a negation) may change the sense. Gap marked where it stands; nothing supplied.

old: Scipio’s statement and his handling of the situation
new: Scipio’s agreement and his handling of the situation
reason: ὁμολογία means agreement or compact (most likely the arrangement with Phameas), not ‘statement’; the fragment breaks off, so the referent is not certain.

old: Thus, stripped of all good things, some perished from hunger, while others, driven to desperation, even then took rods and axes into the cities [...]
new: Thus, stripped of all good things, some [...], while others also [...] into the cities then admitted the rods and axes, willingly [...]
reason: ‘Hunger’ and ‘desperation’ were invented over the gaps (ὑπὸ στέ…, δ…ντες). παρεδέξαντο = admitted. ἐθελο… is broken; ‘willingly’ is likely but not certain.

old: [...] The text here is badly broken in the witness, but the sense is that Polybius is completing Scipio’s remark about the danger of overconfidence and the importance of good judgment.
new: [...] Polybius says [...] that [...] finer than this [...] and this has been said by the poet: [...] And turning at once and grasping my right hand, he said, “Polybius, it is a fine thing; but somehow I fear and foresee that someday someone else will give this same order about our own country.”
reason: Kept the legible fragments and Scipio’s speech, which had been omitted. The quotation the colon announces is missing (marked). The break after ταύτης δὲ falls in the next sentence, outside this span.

old: [...] they were angered at the Roman encampment itself and regretted their former wrongs against themselves [...].
new: [...] of the Roman camp [...] at once regretted [...] the lawless acts committed against them before the Pseudo-Philip [...]. [...] Though they had fought against the Romans with Demetrius, and again with Perseus, and been defeated, yet fighting alongside a hateful man and showing courage for his kingship, they defeated the Romans.
reason: Greek has no ‘angered’. The wrongs were done against them, and the subject of μεταμέλοι is lost. The omitted μὲν…δέ sentence is restored. Δημητρίου is transmitted (Philip V expected): translator’s call.
